chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Isma'il, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about sa'ut (snuff) for the muhrim (one in ihram) in which there is perfume, and he said: There is no objection.
Therefore, the approach in this report is to carry it upon the state of necessity, rather than the state of choice.

key_terms.السَّعُوط: Snuff (powdered incense/spices inhaled through the nose)
key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: For the one in ihram (state of consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a person in ihram to use perfumed snuff?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s permissive ruling on using perfumed snuff (*sa'ut*) for one in *ihram*, which classical jurists interpret as applying primarily to cases of necessity (*darura*) rather than voluntary luxury. This distinction highlights the Shia methodology of balancing textual permissibility with the spirit of ritual purity, ensuring that the use of fragrance does not detract from the solemnity of the pilgrimage state.
